events.label: birth
events.text: Born at Angers, between 1089 and 1092 (earliest year used)

evidence.quote: Fulk was born at Angers , between 1089 and 1092

events.text: Became count of Anjou on his father's death

evidence.quote: Fulk V became count of Anjou upon his fathers death in 1109
was the count of Anjou ( as Fulk V ) from 1109 to 1129
In 1110 , Fulk married Ermengarde of Maine

events.label: alliance
events.text: Allied with Henry I of England; arranged Matilda's marriage to William Adelin (1118 or 1119)

evidence.quote: in 1118 or 1119 he allied with Henry

events.label: crusade
events.text: Went on crusade, became attached to the Knights Templar (1119 or 1120)

evidence.quote: Fulk went on crusade in 1119 or 1120
He returned , late in 1121

events.label: patronage
events.text: Began subsidizing the Knights Templar, maintaining two knights in the Holy Land for a year

evidence.quote: after which he began to subsidize the Templars

events.text: First wife Ermengarde of Maine died

evidence.quote: Ermengarde of Maine ( died 1126 )

events.label: embassy
events.text: Received embassy from Baldwin II about marrying Melisende

evidence.quote: By 1127 Fulk was preparing to return to Anjou when he received an embassy from King Baldwin II of Jerusalem

events.text: Abdicated the county of Anjou to his son Geoffrey

evidence.quote: from 1109 to 1129
Fulk abdicated his county seat of Anjou to his son Geoffrey
where he married Melisende on 2 June 1129

events.text: Became joint ruler (king) of Jerusalem with Melisende

evidence.quote: Fulk and Melisende became joint rulers of Jerusalem in 1131
the king of Jerusalem from 1131 to his death

events.label: battle
events.text: Fought a brief battle with Pons of Tripoli; peace made afterwards

evidence.quote: prevent Fulk from marching north in 1132

events.label: accusation
events.text: Accused Hugh of Jaffa of infidelity with Melisende to expose him

evidence.quote: In 1134 , in order to expose Hugh , Fulk accused him of infidelity with Melisende

events.text: Melisende took direct and unquestioned control of government; Fulk sidelined

In 1137 Fulk was defeated in battle near Baarin but allied with Muin ad-Din Unur

events.label: alliance
events.text: Allied with Muin ad-Din Unur, vizier of Damascus, after defeat near Baarin

evidence.quote: In 1137 Fulk was defeated in battle near Baarin but allied with Muin ad-Din Unur

events.label: death
events.text: Died at Acre after a hunting accident; buried in Jerusalem

evidence.quote: 13 November 1143
In 1143 , while the king and queen were in Acre , Fulk was killed in a hunting accident

undated_mentions: Appointed regent of the Principality of Antioch by Baldwin II
As regent, arranged Raymond of Poitou's marriage to Princess Constance of Antioch
Captured the fort of Banias, north of Lake Tiberias
Had Blanchegarde, Ibelin and other forts built in the south-west
Wrote to Byzantine emperor John II Comnenus that his kingdom could not support a large army (during John's visits in 1137 and 1142)
Agreed to peace with Hugh of Jaffa; Hugh exiled for three years (after 1134)
Fulk or his supporters commonly blamed for an assassination attempt on Hugh of Jaffa
Buried in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem
